mainEntity.name: Why does the output end with =?

acceptedAnswer.text: Padding. Base64 works in groups of 3 bytes. When the input is not a multiple of 3, one or two = characters complete the last group.
A variant that uses - and _ instead of + and /, so it can sit in URLs and file names. JWTs also leave off the = padding.
Every 3 bytes become 4 characters, about 33% larger, plus line breaks if you wrap lines.
No, it is smaller. Base64 grows data by about 33% (3 bytes become 4 characters) while hex doubles it (1 byte becomes 2 characters). A 1 KB input is 1,368 Base64 characters or 2,048 hex characters.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Base64 decode fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usual causes are characters outside the alphabet, a wrong length, missing padding, mixing URL-safe and standard alphabets, or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 text such as an image.

mainEntity.name: Does it handle UTF-8, accents and emoji?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Text is converted to UTF-8 bytes first, so cafe with an accent encodes to Y2Fmw6k= and the grinning-face emoji to 8J+YgA==.

mainEntity.name: How does Base64 work in HTTP Basic authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: The username and password joined by a colon are Base64-encoded, so user:pass becomes dXNlcjpwYXNz. Anyone can decode it, so use HTTPS and never treat it as security.

mainEntity.name: How much bigger does an image become as a data URI?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 33% bigger as Base64. A 10 KB image (10,240 bytes) becomes 13,656 characters, plus the data URI prefix.
